input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: § 7.2 is a reverse MFN: the obligation runs against Customer (Juniper Ridge), requiring us to surface any more favourable third-party commercial offer and match it for Vendor before engaging another provider. That is an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor better terms obtained from third parties, which the playbook treats as unacceptable (walk-away territory) and is inconsistent with § 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer has made no most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is lost by deletion. Preferred remedy: delete § 7.2 entirely; fallback would be an MFN limited to one defined product, 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted § 7.2 because it is a reverse most-favoured-nation obligation requiring us to disclose and match third-party offers for Vendor's benefit; our playbook does not accept MFN obligations running against the customer, and this also conflicts with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in § 12.3. If Vendor needs something here, we could consider an MFN limited to a single defined product for 12 months with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
proposal.summary: Delete reverse MFN obligation on Customer in § 7.2.
